title: The Morning Digest: November 20, 2026
dek: Brent Jan27 settled $91.98, up three cents, and WTI Dec26 settled $83.21, down five cents, on Thursday (Reuters, Nov 19), and Asia bid Brent $92.77 and WTI Jan27 $83.15 at 0404 GMT on Friday (Reuters, Nov 20). December WTI expires today. January WCS settled -$22.00 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 19) on 670 lots, tightening for a third straight session after the December apportionment notice printed Light 24 percent and Heavy 17 percent. The validated diesel crack is $81.29 on the latest print.

sources.vintage: Nov 20, 2026 (overnight tape at 0404 GMT: Brent Jan27 $92.77, up 79 cents or 0.9 percent; WTI Dec26 $83.46, up 25 cents; WTI Jan27 $83.15, up 71 cents or 0.9 percent; both benchmarks set for a third straight weekly loss, Brent down about 3.5 percent and December WTI down almost 6 percent on the week)

Nov 19, 2026 (Thursday settles: Brent Jan27 $91.98, up $0.03; WTI Dec26 $83.21, down $0.05, its lowest settle since Aug 26; WTI Jan27 $82.44, up 0.2 percent, which puts the expiring December premium over January at $0.77 at the settle; Brent prompt spread last reported around $2.40 to $2.80 of backwardation on Nov 17, narrowed from more than $3 a month earlier)

Nov 19, 2026 (TMW Jan27 -$22.00, up $1.45 on 670 lots; Feb27 -$21.55 on 295 lots; Mar27 -$21.20 on 240 lots; Apr27 -$20.45, May27 -$18.90, Jun27 -$17.45; ARV Dec26 -$18.40 on zero lots, Jan27 -$14.40 on 990 lots; January ARV to TMW spread +$7.60; TMS Jan27 +$5.30, TMF Jan27 +$7.00 on 235 lots, TMR Jan27 -$0.75 on 220 lots, TMU Jan27 +$2.80)

Nov 20, 2026 (diesel crack $81.29 and 3-2-1 crack $41.31 on the latest print dated Nov 20; all time maximum diesel crack $117.92 on Sep 16; 45 total closes above $100; current streak above $100 is zero)

Nov 18, 2026 (December Mainline apportionment: Light 24 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 17 percent at Kerrobert; the Cromer and Superior points for December were not found in any public source on the Nov 20 check)

Oct 20, 2026 (standing reference) (November Mainline apportionment: Light 19 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert); the December figures announced Nov 18, 2026 are carried in the December notice chip in this list

Nov 19, 2026 (North Dakota Pipeline chloride disruption ran a sixth day, with flows still suppressed as of Thursday morning on an analyst read; a force majeure at MPLX was reported alongside the earlier Flint Hills Pine Bend report; no restart timeline published)

sources.publisher: Reuters, Nov 19 to 20, 2026 (a Houthi strike damaged the PIF Tower in Riyadh's financial district on Thursday, windows blown out across seven to eight floors, no injuries; Saudi officials reportedly see the Houthi campaign running up to six more months; Houthi claims on Riyadh airport and the SADAF complex at Jubail are unconfirmed and no Saudi oil supply impact was reported)
sources.vintage: unknown

Nov 19, 2026 (seven incidents since the previous update; further attacks rated highly likely in the next 24 to 48 hours; threat level remains SEVERE); JMIC Advisory 017-26, Nov 18, 2026 (the United States blockade wording extended to ship to ship receivers of Iranian cargo)

Nov 19, 2026 (the LPG carrier Tara Gas fire appears under control, with the vessel in a sheltered bay; one seafarer still missing); Reuters, Nov 19, 2026 (Iran's claim that two supertankers hit mines remains unverified, with no vessel named and no corroboration)

Nov 13, 2026 (7d old) (total Hormuz clearance 8,264 kb/d over seven days to Nov 11, 48 percent of the pre-war 17,148 kb/d; total Gulf crude exports including bypass routes ran about 16.7 million barrels a day since Oct 1 against about 17 million pre-war, per Kpler via Reuters, Nov 11; no fresher strait only measured print has been published)

Nov 20, 2026 (the Shenzhen trilateral declaration reaffirmed that a nuclear war must never be fought, promised a dialogue on nuclear risks with no timeframe, and pledged increased fuel supplies with no volumes or mechanism; the declaration did not mention Iran or Ukraine; President Trump said Nov 19 he is not rushing an Iran decision, with the timeline pushed past Jan 1)

Nov 19, 2026 (Russian officials said a drone attack on an oil facility and storage tanks near Almetyevsk in Tatarstan was repelled and a major fire prevented, with no casualties; a separate Reuters follow up frames a possible forced upstream production cut as a risk if refinery and export disruption persist together, not as a confirmed cut)

Nov 18, 2026 (Russian refining processing down about 45 percent point to point since late October on two industry sources, from above 700,000 tonnes a day to about 400,000, with 15 of 35 major refineries disrupted; average November processing above 500,000 tonnes a day, only 5 to 10 percent below September and October, so the 45 percent figure is not a monthly average)

sources.publisher: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report for the week ending
sources.vintage: Nov 13, 2026, released Nov 18, 2026 (crude up 3.380 million barrels to 417.797 million; gasoline up 5.129 million to 215.949 million; distillate up 1.571 million to 104.901 million; Cushing down 1.209 million to 26.147 million; refinery utilisation 95.7 percent; US production 14,032 kb/d; SPR down 3.174 million to 276.361 million, the lowest since August 1982)

Nov 19, 2026 (Pathways talks in their final stretch, with producers unhurried on the missed Nov 15 deadline; Alberta aligned its ACCIP carbon capture incentive with the federal investment tax credit on Nov 19, extended it to 2035, and allowed construction phase funding; no signing announced)

sources.publisher: Baltic Exchange tanker report, Week 46, week ending
sources.vintage: Nov 13, 2026 (7d old) (Gulf of Oman to China VLCC assessment WS310.71; US Gulf Coast to China VLCC lump sum roughly $33.8 million; Caribbean to Gulf Aframax near WS302; the next weekly report, Week 47, is not yet published)
Nov 19, 2026 (fourth quarter VLCC spot bookings at $562,600 a day on 68 percent of days)

sources.publisher: WCSB supply and demand balance build
sources.vintage: Nov 4, 2026 (standing reference) (AER ST3 actuals through September 2026: November supply about 192 kb/d and December about 216 kb/d above the proven egress bound of 4,541.6 kb/d; the balance residual is storage, and the traded strip tightening on volume with an orderly location spread says the residual cannot be read as a storage forecast, because the error sits in one of two named suspects, either the production estimates are too high or the egress capacity is too low; carried forward and checked Nov 20, 2026)

sources.publisher: US Department of Energy, checked directly
sources.vintage: Nov 20, 2026 (no new solicitation, award announcement or posted contract change dated Nov 19 or 20 found; posted contracts have not moved; the latest SPR item remains the Oct 29 award completing the 172 million barrel programme)

Nov 19, 2026 (Goldman Sachs: the Hormuz closure persisted yet prices rose less than expected, because March to October draws were limited to about 600 million barrels by the pre-war surplus and by adaptation; Brent risk premium down from $27 to a few dollars; Brent $92 on average in 2026 and $88 in 2027, easing to $78 by Dec 2027)
